title: Shadow Traffic: payload redaction + config-driven logging allowlists
author: Kevin Osei
release_notes: Internal-only: Shadow runner now redacts request/response payloads before logging/persisting; adds per-tenant allowlists and safe defaults.
description: Problem: Shadow Traffic needs enough request/response context to support judge scoring + debugging, but we cannot persist or emit raw prompts/outputs by default. During beta, several teams also requested explicit controls for what lands in logs vs. analytics events vs. long-term tables. This PR adds a first-class redaction layer and config-driven allowlists for all shadow payload handling. Scope: (1) Add a PayloadRedactor module applied in the shadow runner before any event is enqueued/persisted/emitted. (2) Introduce redaction + logging controls in ShadowTrafficConfig with safe defaults (store_mode=none, log_mode=metadata_only). (3) Add PII detectors (regex-based) for common patterns (email, phone, CC, SSN-like, IPv4/IPv6) + configurable custom regexes per tenant, and deterministic hashing for correlation. (4) Enforce attribute allowlists for telemetry tags/trace attributes to prevent accidental prompt leakage. (5) Add audits: any attempt to enable raw payload storage requires an explicit tenant override + feature gate, and writes an audit log entry with actor + reason. Non-goals: Perfect PII detection; this is a guardrail and default-safe system. Detailed changes: - New config keys (control plane surfaced; data plane reads via cached policy bundle): shadow_traffic.payload.store_mode: none|redacted|raw (raw blocked unless tenant_override + shadow_raw_payloads feature gate), shadow_traffic.payload.redaction_profile: default|strict|custom, shadow_traffic.logging.log_mode: off|metadata_only|redacted_payload (default metadata_only), shadow_traffic.logging.allowlisted_fields: list of JSON pointer paths that may be retained in redacted payload snapshots (default empty). - Redaction behavior: Removes message/content fields by default; if allowlisted, content is redacted in-place using detectors and then truncated to max 2KB per field. Adds stable hash fields (sha256 w/ per-tenant salt from KMS) for: prompt_hash, output_hash to support dedup + join without storing raw text. - Telemetry: shadow_eval.* events now run through attribute allowlist: request_id, route_id, model, region, sampling_pct, judge_version, plus redacted_payload_present boolean; blocks arbitrary headers/body fields even if present upstream. - Logging: Introduces a separate "restricted" logger channel for redaction diagnostics that is disabled in prod by default; when enabled, logs only counts and detector matches (no substrings). - Tests: unit tests for detectors, truncation, and hashing stability; integration test verifying no prompt content reaches telemetry exporter; regression test for policy hot-reload on allowlist changes. Risk/Perf: Redaction runs in the shadow path only; primary path untouched. Shadow runner redaction adds ~0.2–0.6ms per shadowed request for typical payload sizes in local benchmark; includes max-bytes guard to short-circuit very large payloads (drop_payload=true + metric increment). Follow-ups: console UI for per-tenant overrides and a self-serve "redaction preview" is tracked separately. Review notes requested: please focus on default safety and any paths where raw payload might bypass redaction (queue replay, judge input construction, sampling debug logs).
commits: shadow-runner: add PayloadRedactor and wire into enqueue + telemetry emit
config: introduce ShadowTraffic payload/logging controls with safe defaults
security: add per-tenant salt hashing via KMS-backed keyring
telemetry: enforce attribute allowlist + drop-on-violation behavior
tests: redaction detector suite + no-leak integration test
ci_checks: perf-canary/shadow-overhead — pass (rerun required once due to flaky runner)
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we guarantee no raw prompt tokens hit trace attributes? I see we attach request.body_size_bytes; but do we ever attach request.body anywhere else through default middleware? Also please add a hard fail if a blocked attribute key is set (metric + drop).

Kevin Osei (author): Good catch. The shadow runner was inheriting generic http middleware attributes; I added a sanitize step to strip http.request.body.* and any attribute not in allowlist before export. Also added shadow_eval.attribute_blocked_count metric and we drop the attribute + log (counts only). Pushed commit 5f2a9d1.

Logan Wright: Telemetry side: do we need prompt_hash/output_hash at all? It’s useful but adds join surface area. If we keep it, make sure the salt is per-tenant and rotates safely. Also please ensure these hashes never become dimensions on metrics (only event fields).

Kevin Osei (author): Agreed. Hashes are written only in the shadow_eval.run event payload and excluded from metric tag allowlist. Salt is derived from tenant_key_id in KMS; rotation invalidates historical correlations (acceptable). Added docs note + tests that metrics exporter rejects these keys.

Marcus Lin: Redaction detectors: regex SSN/CC can be noisy. Do we have an escape hatch for customers who want "strict" (remove everything) vs "default" (pattern replace) vs "custom"? Also, raw storage path must be behind two gates (config + server-side allow).

Kevin Osei (author): Implemented redaction_profile enum (default/strict/custom). Strict drops all allowlisted text fields entirely (sets to null, preserves shape). Raw storage now requires: (1) tenant_override.shadow_raw_payloads=true in control plane, (2) feature gate shadow_raw_payloads enabled, and (3) store_mode=raw. Otherwise validation downgrades to redacted and emits shadow_eval.store_mode_downgraded_count.

Naomi Feldman: Compliance: default must be store_mode=none, log_mode=metadata_only. Also we need an audit log entry whenever raw is enabled (who/why). Please ensure debug logging can’t accidentally print substrings; counts only.

Kevin Osei (author): Defaults set as requested. Added audit event ShadowRawPayloadsEnabled with actor_id + reason + time, emitted from control plane on policy update. Shadow runner restricted logger prints only detector match counts and total bytes dropped. No substring logging.

Dylan Brooks: Judge input construction: do we run judge on raw content or redacted content? If we judge on redacted content we’ll lose signal; if we judge on raw, we must ensure raw never lands in persistence. Please clarify.

Kevin Osei (author): Judge runs on in-memory raw shadow response (not persisted). Redaction is applied only to anything leaving the worker process (queue payload, events, logs). Added comment + guard: judge prompt is built before redaction, and we explicitly zero out raw buffers after judge completion when feasible. Added integration test asserting persisted event does not include message.content.
Allison Grant: Last ask: add a dashboard/alert hook for redaction drops (payload too large / invalid UTF8) so SRE can see if this is hiding issues.
Kevin Osei (author): Added shadow_eval.payload_dropped_total (reason=too_large|invalid_utf8|redaction_error) and included in the existing shadow runner overview dashboard list. Pushed commit a8c31bf.
Naomi Feldman: Approved after audit logging landed and defaults verified.
